Associate returned pages with their requested URLs and build extraction evidence from successful cached results. Reuse cached text directly for subsequent extraction and quote-membership checks. Exclude FETCH_FAILED results from usable evidence. This procedure applies when the cached rendering supplies the evidence needed for the current focus; cache presence alone does not establish relevance or completeness.

proposal.summary: Retain existing fetch-recovery guidance; refine discovery deduplication and semantic completeness checks with two targeted updates.

edits.title: Inspect results and resolve aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, do this separately for each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier event. Compare entity identities, not just exact name strings: punctuation variants, omitted initials, and contextually identified surnames can refer to already known entities. Maintain evidence-supported aliases without merging ambiguous names. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including verification searches that supply new field evidence. Do not invent discoveries or count known aliases as new entities to suppress stall warnings.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered pages
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing or incomplete fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries with brief supporting excerpts rather than full-page reproduction. Test a revised focus on one page and inspect its evidence before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus so later responses do not overwrite earlier support. Before new retrieval, review saved evidence for fields an extraction omitted. Keep unstated fields unresolved and use alternative sources instead of inferring facts from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotes against an individual saved response, then separately check that they support the correct entity, field, time, and full requested scope. A nonempty value and matching quote do not establish completeness: flag summaries or excerpts when exact wording is required, and verify attribution of shared statements. Track these semantic gaps alongside empty cells; do not insert editorial gap notes into factual values. Retrieve only the unresolved evidence, repair affected cells, and repeat both membership and semantic checks. Match the task's evidence contract: rendered-text membership does not authenticate a quotation against raw source text. FETCH_FAILED calls for bounded retries and source switching instead.

additional_candidates.description: Exact-string novelty checks counted name variants and surnames of known entities as new discoveries.
Semantic review recovered omitted evidence and incomplete populated fields that passed quote-membership checks.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel URLs, then LIGO, EurekAlert, Campus France, Scientific American, Le Monde, Tokyo, three Nature pages, a CV, and Leopoldina. The run tracked attempted URLs, tested a small alternative-source batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through usable alternative evidence, including another CV and an APS source. The discoveries ledger labels omitted-initial variants, apostrophe variants, and later bare surnames as new_entities after the corresponding people were already discovered. The trajectory uses exact-string set membership. Final row deduplication recovered output coverage, but discovery accounting remained inflated. Extend the existing discovery memory with evidence-supported identity resolution.

Quote checks repeatedly passed while an exact-motivation field remained an excerpt; later even the empty-cell check passed with an editorial incompleteness note in that value. Semantic audits also found usable saved evidence omitted by extraction and attribution problems in shared quotations. Targeted retrieval and repair resolved these before final validation. Extend the existing recovery skill with this successful audit procedure; its empty usage/outcome history provides no basis for deletion.

proposal.summary: Preserve existing discovery and quotation guidance, clarify review scope, and add a memory preventing verification from discarding stronger evidence.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Pass the task's field definitions, time frame, and chosen source scope to extraction and review calls. If the task leaves scope ambiguous, make the working interpretation explicit and consistent. Assess reviewer suggestions against that scope before expanding research; for announcement-listed affiliations, unrelated advisory appointments are not omissions. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Compare verification results before replacing supported cells
edits.content: A follow-up extraction using narrower evidence replaced a supported multi-valued nationality with a single country from another person's page navigation. Schema and quote-membership checks passed despite the loss; the original evidence had to be restored. Supply the existing cell and its supporting evidence to verification calls. Stage proposed replacements and compare their scope, completeness, source relevance, and temporal meaning before committing them. A source mentioning only one value does not disprove other supported values, and a failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate evidence already collected. Preserve supported values unless stronger evidence explicitly corrects them; investigate genuine conflicts rather than blindly replacing or unioning results.

additional_candidates.description: Carry field definitions and source scope into semantic review to prevent unrelated affiliation investigations.
Prevent follow-up extraction from replacing stronger, complete evidence with a narrower supported subset.
Repair noncontiguous PDF quotations using exact stored source slices.

The coordinator clarified that the working scope was affiliations recorded in award announcements; the final scoped review passed. Updating the existing biographical-review skill preserves this successful procedure without hardcoding that interpretation for every task. Its recorded outcome is successful, so targeted clarification is warranted rather than deletion.

The coordinator committed that narrower cell, reported no structural or quotation errors, then explicitly restored the stronger original evidence. Final citation checks passed after recovery, but they do not prevent this semantic loss. Existing entries cover missing fields and quotation repair, not replacement regressions, so a separate failure memory is justified.

An affiliation quotation failed membership because it reconstructed interleaved PDF text incorrectly. The coordinator located and copied a contiguous source slice, and final citation checks passed. Entry 1 already describes this exact failure, repair, and revalidation procedure. Its successful outcome provides no reason to revise or duplicate it.

proposal.summary: Update two existing memories to prevent repeated retrieval of absent fields and keep semantic audits aligned with the requested column. Existing entries already cover honest discovery logging and fetch-failure recovery.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, labels and assembled passages; do not reject a genuine source heading merely because the tool renders it. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, applicable time period and every substantive component of the value. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested column: an explicit national descriptor can support nationality without establishing legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Treat reviewer findings as hypotheses to resolve against supplied evidence, not instructions to strengthen the task's requirements. For affiliations, distinguish separately affiliated institutions from parenthetical parent-organization descriptions. When sources support different parts of a composite claim, retain an internal claim-to-excerpt mapping and respect the output contract rather than stitching excerpts into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

edits.title: Probe source availability and track field coverage
edits.content: When prior run evidence reports uniform fetch failures on a host, test one or two returned URLs before committing another large batch to that host. Recheck availability rather than assuming a permanent outage. After a uniformly failed batch, inspect saved search hits for authoritative alternative hosts and probe one or two URLs before expanding fetching or repeating discovery searches. Preserve search results and successful fetched text, track failed URLs, and avoid unchanged failed batches. Changing to same-host PDFs does not establish recovery; ordinary URLs and unusual suffixes both failed, so the cause remains unknown. Treat FETCH_FAILED as unavailable evidence, never citation text. Track field coverage separately from fetch status: a successful retrieval can explicitly report that a requested field is absent. Consult those absence notes before another focused fetch; seek a different source unless there is a concrete reason to believe the earlier retrieval omitted relevant material. Preserve each successful retrieval separately, including its focus and field limitations, so later failures or narrower results do not overwrite usable evidence. Expand only after inspecting probe results; proposed fallback calls are not evidence of recovery.

additional_candidates.description: Audits temporarily substituted citizenship for nationality and treated an organizational parenthetical as a missing affiliation; later reviews corrected these interpretations.
Eight focused nationality fetches revisited pages whose saved extractions already reported no explicit nationality or citizenship, and all eight confirmed absence.
Preserving retrieval versions and validating targeted patches supported recovery without discarding earlier usable quotations.

decisions.reason: All 29 occurrences were considered. The first four are fallback searches that yielded no new names after initial discovery; the remaining nine nationality, eleven gap, and five targeted searches investigated already known entities. Their empty discovery records are consistent with that purpose, and several yielded useful evidence despite no entity growth. Entry 0 already requires inspection before logging and explicitly permits honest empty records for verification. Its repeated signal counts therefore do not establish consistently bad behavior or justify suppressing legitimate verification searches.

All 26 failures were considered: nine initial same-host failures, six failures in the expanded alternative-source batch, seven in nationality retrieval, two in gap retrieval, and two in final targeted retrieval. These include repeat failures for the LIGO and AP URLs and a later failure for an APS URL that had previously succeeded. Recovery through successful alternative hosts is visible. Entry 1's current version already addresses prior-host probes, failed-URL tracking, preservation of successful evidence, and avoiding unsupported explanations for failures; its usage records concern the earlier version. No additional failure-specific rule is needed, and passing checks alone are not the reason for declining.

The second audit explicitly demanded citizenship evidence for nationality cells, while later prompts restored the distinction and accepted explicit national descriptors. A post-patch affiliation audit also demanded a parent organization, then a focused resolution retained the supported institutions. These recovered review errors expose ambiguity in entry 3's combined nationality/citizenship guidance. Clarifying the existing memory preserves its useful semantic checks without treating reviewer assertions or deterministic citation membership as factual authority.

Earlier saved extractions explicitly reported absent nationality/citizenship for all eight revisited announcement pages. Fetch records 49–56 and their trajectory results confirm that every subsequent nationality-only retrieval repeated that absence. Later alternative-source searches supplied the missing evidence. Extend entry 1 from transport availability to field coverage, allowing justified focused retries while avoiding this repeated unproductive batch.

The run preserved page_versions, checked quotations against individual saved retrievals, and validated targeted patches before applying them. Final checks passed, although semantic review remained necessary. Entry 2 already covers saved-evidence repair, complete-value support and validation before mutation; retrieval preservation is also retained in the availability update. A separate skill would duplicate this coverage, so the edit budget favors the two concrete failure-mode clarifications.

proposal.summary: Preserve field-specific supplementation as a skill and record the observed temporal-normalization failure as a memory. Retain the existing discovery guidance: all 35 stalled-search signals are compatible with honest empty discovery reports. Fetch failures had alternate-source coverage. The snapshot lacks final submission, but does not establish that the ongoing run abandoned finalization.

edits.title: Supplement missing fields with explicit evidence
edits.content: For multi-entity research, extract supported fields from authoritative overview sources into schema-validated records, retaining source URLs and exact quotations. Keep unsupported fields explicitly missing. Build follow-up queries only for missing entity-field pairs and group related evidence for extraction. Prefer sources that explicitly state the requested attribute; source prestige, birthplace, ancestry, residence, or institutional location cannot substitute for that statement. Preserve supported multiplicity and original-language quotations when translating values. A failed download is unavailable evidence: use an accessible alternative for the unresolved field, and do not cite the failed page or its search snippet as fetched support. Validate returned entity identities, coverage, and quote membership before merging supplemental cells by entity key. Treat successful extraction as intermediate work; complete semantic review and the required final output separately.

edits.title: Exact quotations do not resolve temporal ambiguity
edits.content: An extraction reproduced a nationality label exactly but converted its mixture of historical and present-day country terminology into an unqualified contemporary multiple-nationality claim. Quote membership verifies textual fidelity, not the full meaning of the normalized value. Before accepting a cell, check that the quoted passage supports the subject, requested attribute, every component of the value, and relevant time. Do not silently convert a historical state or a parenthetical modern geographic label into current citizenship. Preserve the source's qualification, seek explicit corroboration, or leave the unsupported component unresolved under the output contract.

additional_candidates.description: Schema-validated overview extraction exposed missing nationality fields; grouped biography extraction supplied explicit supplemental evidence, including multilingual and multiple-nationality statements.
An exact supporting quotation with mixed historical/current terminology was normalized into an unqualified contemporary multiple-nationality value.
A fallback URL selector reintroduced an excluded mirror, alternate-format fetching mostly repeated evidence, and a large biography fetch batch consumed substantial time.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty_output, with empty citations and constraint coverage. However, the trajectory ends at five completed subordinate extraction responses following code that requests this refinement; no subsequent root completion or terminal failure is recorded. The last completed worker iteration has null final_answer, which is expected during research. This establishes missing submission at this snapshot, not an observed failure to finalize a completed run. The base instructions already require serialization and readiness assignment. No additional finalization memory is justified without a terminal outcome.

All 35 occurrences were compared with their search results and discovery calls. Signals 0–8 concern overview hits whose titles/snippets did not name new laureates; their empty reports followed inspection. Signal 9 concerns an already-recorded entity during source recovery. Signals 10–34 concern field supplementation for the 25 entities already extracted into rows, so populated hits did not imply newly discovered entities. These searches produced useful sources despite zero new-entity reports. The existing memory explicitly permits honest empty reports for verification searches and forbids fabricated discoveries. Its usage and outcomes arrays are empty, providing no evidence of consistently harmful outcomes. Retain it unchanged rather than treating these signals as repeated placeholder failures.

All ten failures were reviewed: six HTTP access failures, three redirect loops, and one broken-pipe download error. Signal 35's mirror failure recovered through an official PDF, whose extracted rows passed quote assertions and were incorporated. Signals 36–44 affected biography sources, but the completed supplemental responses selected accessible alternatives for every affected entity: Smith, Henderson, Winter, Whittingham, Charpentier (two failed sources), List, MacMillan, and Stoddart. This supports field-level alternate-source coverage, not claims that failed endpoints were repaired or that an adaptive retry occurred. Preserve the reusable alternative-source procedure within the supplementation skill; do not blacklist domains or prescribe unsupported retries.

The overview extraction diagnostic records 25 missing nationality cells and no quote-membership errors; recovered PDF extraction adds supported rows. All five subsequent biography responses provide structured supplemental candidates using explicit field statements rather than birthplace or affiliation. Independent inspection of the recorded captures confirms quotation membership for all 140 populated extracted cells. This is a repeatable acquisition/extraction tactic, including multilingual and multiple-value evidence, but the snapshot does not demonstrate the planned aggregate validation, merge, or final submission. The skill preserves those boundaries and requires validation before merging.

The response in trajectory/76 turns a label combining a historical state and parenthetical modern terminology into an unqualified contemporary multiple-nationality value. Its quotation is an exact substring, so the planned membership check in trajectory/71 would not detect the lost qualification. The prompt already cautioned against historical/current conflation, yet this candidate remained ambiguous and no correction is recorded. Preserve the failure mode and require semantic and temporal support separately from quotation fidelity, without storing the task's answer facts.

The URL fallback in trajectory/8 fails to retain its mirror exclusion and selects a mirror that fails; a targeted search subsequently recovers an official PDF. The PDF sweep mostly duplicates already acquired fields, and the biography batch returns 75 results with nine failures after about 601 seconds. These are real efficiency signals, but no timeout or exhausted budget is shown, and alternate sources yielded useful supplementation. With two edits available, prioritize the demonstrated field-supplementation procedure and semantic normalization failure over a separate selector or batching entry. The skill already limits follow-up work to unresolved entity-field pairs.
